messages:
ren: Quick dump from onboarding OrpheusX-compact (int4). Two surprises: a block-stride head layout (blocks of 4 interleaved) that causes KV-cache wrap/offsets at long context (~2k tokens), and a punctuation normalization problem where exporter applied NFKC and collapsed a few punctuation variants causing shadowing in the embedding table. Leaving notes here.
hannah: Numbers and conversion command?
ren: Baselines: fp16 ppl 1.78 on conv-eval, int8 1.82, int4 before fixes 3.2. Summarize ROUGE-L fp16 43.1, int4 pre-fix 30. Command: 
```
python3 tools/convert_model.py \
  --src-format orpheusx \
  --dst-format gemma-compatible \
  --quant int4 \
  --vocab-map maps/orpheusx_to_gemma_nfkc.json \
  --out /tmp/orp_gemma_int4
```
ren: tokenmap snippet around punctuation: 
```
{"821":"821","822":"822","823":"823","824":"824","825":"824"}
# note: src ids 824 and 825 both map -> 824 after exporter NFKC normalization of U+2019 vs U+0027
```
omar: interesting. The head layout you describe doesn't look like even-odd; looks like block interleave. Did you correlate head signatures?
ren: I dumped rotary/QK head blocks (fp32 pre-quant) and computed pairwise cosine. Found pattern: heads are laid out in blocks of 4 that were written as block0_even, block1_even, block0_odd, block1_odd etc. Inferred perm for H heads (H multiple of 4): 
```
# block interleave -> contiguous
B = 4
perm = []
for b in range(B):
    for i in range(H//B):
        perm.append(b + i*B)
# apply: tensor = tensor[perm]
```
omar: So exporter wrote by intra-block stride. Did you try reordering before quant?
ren: Yes. Applied perm to rotary, q/k/v/o, and LN affine params before int4. Also fixed the tokenmap by reverting NFKC normalization for a small set of punctuation (kept native codepoints). After both fixes: int4 ppl 1.86, ROUGE-L 42.8 — basically recovered. Isolated effects: just block-reorder -> ppl 1.92, ROUGE-L 41.5; just vocab revert -> ppl 2.6, ROUGE-L 36.7. So both mattered.
lena: The Unicode/NFKC collapse is subtle. Some upstream exporters auto-normalize text/vocab; if they normalize right before writing the vocab indices, multiple distinct source graphemes can collapse to one target id. That kills embedding diversity for punctuation-heavy tasks (summaries, chats). We should add a tokenmap sanity check asserting injectivity for small ranges (punctuation, currency, quotes).
hannah: Also we saw KV wrap/offset at long context; how reproducible?
ren: Repro shows KV-cache position offsets skew after ~2048 tokens: attention attends to older positions as if head stride moved. Fixing block-order eliminated the wrap. I also verified with long-context stress test (prompt length 4096) and the reorder keeps attention offsets aligned across the full range.
omar: Can we add auto-detect heuristics: 1) head-block correlation test (detect block-size by scanning for repeated pattern), 2) tokenmap injectivity test over punctuation and common clusters, 3) long-context KV smoke test. If detected, auto-apply fixes or fail conversion with clear hint.
ren: Plan: will submit PR with: --fix-head-block (auto-detect + explicit override), --preserve-unicode (disable exporter NFKC passthrough), tools/check_block_head_layout.py (emits perm + heatmap), tools/check_tokenmap_injectivity.py, and a CI microtest: convert tiny model slice, run seed prompts (16 tokens + 4096 stress) and compute attention-position correlation; fail if corr drop >8% vs fp16. Will add model-catalog metadata: 
["rotary_layout"] = "contiguous|block-4|block-8|unknown", 
["unicode_normalization"] = "NFKC|NFC|none"
ops-bot: ticket INF-4102 created: "OrpheusX-compact: block-head interleave + unicode punct collapse" assigned to ren, priority P2.
hannah: Also log exporter version (exporter_git_sha) and include the original raw vocab file in conversion artifacts so we can audit normalization.
ren: Will do. I'll attach before/after head dumps and the tokenmap diffs to the PR. Thx everyone. :thumbsup:
